### Time limits now appear on Home
The list along the bottom of Home showed instant blocks, always-on blocks and scheduled ones, but never a time limit — so a limit that was quietly counting down had nothing on screen to say so.
It is there now, and it counts the right thing: while you still have budget it shows what is left of your allowance; once the budget is spent it switches to counting the block down. A limit whose block has already run and expired drops off the list, because those apps are open again until tomorrow and a row reading "0m" would say the opposite.
The Blocker card no longer keeps a stale count after you stop a session, and the list itself folds away from a handle on its bottom edge rather than a button sitting in a strip of its own.
### Choosing how long a limit blocks for
The screen that asks how long to block for after a limit runs out has been rebuilt. It opens on "Until tomorrow", offers the common lengths as one tap, and keeps the hours and minutes fields for anything else.
A schedule or a time limit can no longer be saved with no day selected — it would never have run, and nothing said so.
### Managed Macs
On a Mac managed by an organisation or by a parent, the protection level is no longer the device's to change. "No Protection" sits inside that chooser, so reaching it was a way out of the policy, one tap from Home, for exactly the person the policy is meant to protect. Setting up Safe Internet still works, and your administrator still chooses the level.
Policy changes also arrive as soon as the app comes back to the front, rather than waiting for the next check.
